newsitem.title: UK: IGC raises 1996 wheat crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: IGC raises 1996 wheat crop estimate.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday raised its estimate for 1996 world wheat production to 580 million tonnes, from a previous estimate made in November of 575 million.
The rise mainly reflected increased estimates for Canada, Australia and Russia.
In its latest market report, the IGC left its estimate for stocks unchanged at 102 million tonnes.

The rise in production includes an extra 1.2 million tonnes for the former USSR, mostly accounted for by a rise for Russia to 34.9 million tonnes from the previous estimate of 34.0 million, which compared with the IGC's estimate for 1995 of 30.1 million.

The overall rise also includes an extra two million tonnes for Australia, where production is put at 23 million tonnes, compared with the previous estimate of 21.0 million and a 1995 figure of 17 million.
The IGC upped its estimate for Canadian wheat production to 30.5 million tonnes from November's 29.5 million and 1995 output of 25.4 million.
The IGC raised its estimate of 1996 wheat production in Iraq to 1.4 million tonnes from a previous figure of one million.
